title.value: The Variational Bandwidth Bottleneck: Stochastic Evaluation on an Information Budget
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the beginning of the document as 'The Variational Bandwidth Bottleneck: Stochastic Evaluation on an Information Budget'.
title.quote: THE VARIATIONAL BANDWIDTH BOTTLENECK: STOCHASTIC EVALUATION ON AN INFORMATION BUDGET

analysis.description: This paper introduces the concept of the Variational Bandwidth Bottleneck (VBB), a method that decides for each example on the estimated value of privileged information before seeing it. This approach is applied to reinforcement learning tasks to improve generalization and reduce the access to costly information.

type.justification: The paper provides experimental evaluations and applications of the proposed VBB method in reinforcement learning tasks, showing empirical results.
type.quote: In this work, we propose the variational bandwidth bottleneck, which decides for each example on the estimated value of the privileged information before seeing it, i.e., only based on the standard input, and then accordingly chooses stochastically, whether to access the privileged input or not. We formulate a tractable approximation to this framework and demonstrate in a series of reinforcement learning experiments that it can improve generalization and reduce access to computationally costly information.

name.justification: The primary focus of the paper is on applying the VBB method to reinforcement learning to construct agents that can dynamically decide when to use privileged information.
name.quote: For example, in reinforcement learning, which is the primary subject of our experiments, the agent can be augmented with some privileged information in the form of a model based planner, or information which is the result of communication with another agent.

name.justification: The paper relies on concepts from information theory, such as the information bottleneck and mutual information, which are central to the development of the VBB method.
name.quote: The information bottleneck method formalizes this as an information-theoretic optimization problem by maintaining an optimal tradeoff between compression (throwing away irrelevant input information), and predicting the target.

name.justification: The paper discusses applications of the VBB method in multi-agent communication scenarios.
name.quote: Next, we consider multiagent communication, where in order to solve a task, agents must communicate with other agents.
